One solid glyph per observation

Source: R/layers-glyph.R
geom_glyph_3d.Rd

Places a copy of a small mesh at each x, y, z, as Makie's meshscatter and PyVista's glyph() do. Built-in glyphs are "sphere", "cube", "cone", "cylinder" and "octahedron", all centred on the origin and spanning -1 to 1 along each axis; any mesh_3d() or rgl mesh3d object can be used instead, with its origin at the observation. The glyphs are solids in the panel scene: they intersect other geometry exactly and take light.

Usage

geom_glyph_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = "identity",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  glyph = "sphere",
  size.unit = "mm",
  detail = 2L,
  shade = TRUE,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

glyph

A built-in glyph name or a mesh from mesh_3d() or read_mesh_3d().

size.unit

Unit of the size aesthetic: "mm" or "data".

detail

Tessellation level of the built-in round glyphs, from 0 to 6.

shade

Whether to apply lighting.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

The size aesthetic is the width of a built-in glyph: a mesh is scaled by size / 2. With size.unit = "mm" (the default) it is measured on screen at the centre of the view, so a mapped size follows the usual size scale; with size.unit = "data" it is measured in the scale-transformed units of each position axis (use ggplot2::scale_size_identity() to keep mapped values as they are) and the glyphs expand the position scales.

The optional u, v and w aesthetics give a direction in data units; the glyph's z axis, the apex of the cone, turns to follow it. Cones and cylinders have 8 * 2^detail sides; spheres are icospheres of 20 * 4^detail triangles.

See also

geom_sphere_3d(), geom_ellipsoid_3d().

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = 1:3, y = 1:3, z = 1)
d$u <- d$y - 2; d$v <- 2 - d$x; d$w <- 1
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, u = u, v = v, w = w)) +
  geom_glyph_3d(glyph = "cone", size = 6, fill = "tomato") + coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg, z = qsec, size = hp, fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_glyph_3d(glyph = "cube") + coord_3d()
